application_process:
Application Procedure:
The application may be made online through using the Registration/login Page of "
Culture Scheme Monitoring System (CSMS) (http://csms.nic.in/login/index.php)
" on the 
website of the Ministry of Culture (https://indiaculture.gov.in)
 under the heading of "MOC Schemes Application".
Selection of Applicants for Award of Artists Pension:
Step 01:
 The applications of eligible artists found to be complete in all respects will be placed before Expert Committee constituted by the Ministry of Culture under the Scheme after getting physical inspection/verification of the applicants done by officer(s) of the Ministry of Culture or one of the organizations of Ministry of Culture.
Step 02:
 The Expert Committee will consider the applications in terms of extant guidelines of the Scheme and recommend the names of deserving candidates for the award of Artists' Pension solely on merit considering the financial position and eminence etc. of the applicant artist.
Step 03:
 The recommendations of the Expert Committee are to be examined by the Administration Division with reference to the Scheme guidelines and the rules of the Govt. as also the availability of funds under the Scheme to facilitate an appropriate decision by the Competent Authority.
Step 04:
 The cases of all the recommended candidates will be submitted finally for getting approval of the Competent Authority which will be one level above the Chairperson of the Expert Committee. Before the release of financial assistance to the approved candidates, the concurrence of the Internal Finance Division shall be obtained.
Disbursement of artist's pension:
Monthly Artist Pension to the approved existing beneficiaries (i.e. pensioner) and new artists to be included in the beneficiaries list subsequent to the recommendation of the Expert Committee and thereafter approval of the Competent Authority, will be disbursed by the Ministry of Culture through Public Financial Management System (PFMS)/Direct Benefit Transfer(DBT) or through Service Provider (appointed by Ministry of Culture for disbursement of Artists Pension) directly into their bank account subject to receiving the following documents mandatorily online on the email of Artistes Pension Section of the Ministry i.e. documents.moc@gmail.com or artistspension.moc@gmail.com and after examination/scrutiny, the same are found to be in order:
Every Year in November, the Digital Life Certificate (DLC) of the beneficiary is processed through the Jeevan Pramaan Portal (https://jeevanpramaan.gov.in) by using necessary information like Aadhaar number, Mobile number, and Pension Payment Order (PPO) displayed by the Ministry on its website [Till the time the Aadhaar Card is made mandatory by the Government for an individual residing in the State of Assam, Meghalaya, and Jammu & Kashmir, they may submit a colored scanned copy of their original Life Certificate]; and
Every Five (05) Years, a Coloured scanned copy of the original Income Certificate in the prescribed format is issued by the concerned Competent Authority of the States/UTs. The beneficiaries will have to furnish any other requisite information/document(s) as sought by the Ministry from time to time. In case the requisite documents sought by the Ministry are not received from a beneficiary, the pension will not be released to him/her. Further, if any discrepancy is found in the documents furnished by the beneficiary, the pension may not be released or stopped forthwith till such time the discrepancy is rectified.
Renewal of financial assistance to existing beneficiaries:
Subject to the above provisions the recurring monthly allowance sanctioned under the Scheme to the existing beneficiaries shall be for such period as may be determined by the Central Government and/or may be continued on a year-to-year basis on receipt of Digital Life Certificate (DLC) and Income Certificate from them.
Discontinuance of allowance:
If the financial means of a recipient improve beyond ₹4000/- (Rupees four thousand only) per month or annual income of ₹48,000/- (Rupees forty-eight thousand only) [This excludes artiste pension assistance amount already getting by a beneficiary from the Government (i.e. concerned State Govt./UT Administration and/or Ministry of Culture)], allowance under the Scheme will be discontinued forthwith without any notice to the recipient. The government may also at its discretion terminate the allowance after giving three months' notice to the recipient.
       Any recipient may also relinquish his/her right to receive allowance by giving written notice to the Government. In such cases, the allowance will be discontinued with effect from the date of his/ her letter of relinquish.

description: The scheme "Scheme for Financial Assistance to Select States/UTs for Skill Development in ESDM Sector" has been launched by the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology, Government of India. It aims at enhancing the skilling capacities in the ESDM sector through the public and private sectors for students/unemployed youth belonging to other disciplines by utilising the existing human resources who are undergoing studies in schools (IX standard onwards)/ITIs/Polytechnics/UG Colleges (non-engineering) and the school dropouts/unemployed youth by providing them with additional skills that are recognised by industry for employment in the ESDM sector, Encouraging new investments in training in the ESDM sector by the industry, Facilitating the evolution of processes/norms for: Certification of various courses; Providing opportunities for moving up the value chain; and Recognition of institutions for conducting such courses, as per the requirements of the industry in the ESDM sector > **Objectives:** - To provide financial assistance for facilitating skill development for 90,000 persons in the ESDM sector by involving select States/UTs for improving the employability of the students/unemployed youth.

application_process:
Registration:
Step 1: 
Visit the official ESDM Skill Development portal: 
https://esdm-skill.deity.gov.in. (https://esdm-skill.deity.gov.in)
Step 2: 
Identify the nearest affiliated Training Partner (TP) through the portal or authorised sources.
Step 3: 
Approach the Training Partner for counselling and selection of the appropriate NSQF course.
Step 4: 
Submit required documents and eligibility details to the Training Partner.
Step 5: 
Provide Aadhaar Number or Aadhaar Enrolment ID and complete Aadhaar authentication / e-KYC (with consent).
Step 6: 
Fill the application/enrolment form at the Training Partner centre or through the portal.

Pay the Registration-cum-Certification Fee (RCCF) to the Training Partner.
Step 8: 
Submit required undertakings:
Undertaking for the non-availability of a similar Government scheme
Undertaking for willingness for employment/self-employment
Step 9:
The Training Partner verifies eligibility and completes enrolment of the applicant.
After Registration:

The applicant undergoes training for the prescribed duration as per the selected NSQF course.
Step 2: 
The applicant maintains the required attendance (minimum 70%) during training.
Step 3: 
The applicant appears for assessment conducted by the respective Key Implementing Agency (KIA).
Step 4: 
Upon successful assessment, the applicant receives certification.
Step 5: 
The Training Partner facilitates placement or supports self-employment opportunities.
Step 6: 
Placement of the candidate is tracked for a minimum period of 3 months.
Step 7: 
Financial reimbursement is processed:
First instalment after certification
Second instalment after successful placement

scheme_name_original: Scheme for Grant of Financial Assistance for Administering Road Safety Advocacy and Awards for the Outstanding Work Done in the Field of Road Safety
description:
The scheme “Scheme for Grant of Financial Assistance for Administering Road Safety Advocacy and Awards for the Outstanding Work Done in the Field of Road Safety” was launched by the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways, Government of India. The objective of the Scheme is to stimulate and encourage opportunities for various agencies through participation, in order to create awareness on road safety. The Scheme will work in alignment with the following objectives of the National Road Safety Policy-

  - To evolve a shared vision of priorities and strategies in promoting road safety.
  - To foster cooperative federalism through support initiatives and mechanisms with the States on a continuous basis.
  - To develop and ensure credible plans for financial assistance to various stakeholders for administering road safety programmes and raising awareness about road safety issues through education, training, and publicity campaigns.
  - To design strategic, long-term policies, programme, and initiatives, and monitor their progress and their efficacy. The lessons learned through monitoring and feedback will be used for making innovative improvements.
  - To create a knowledge base through best practices and good governance in sustainable and equitable development.
  - To facilitate recognition and award to partners for their initiatives and recommendable work in the field of road safety.

eligibility_summary:
1. The Applicant Agency shall be an NGO/Trust under the Indian Trusts Act/Cooperative Society under the Societies Registration Act/Firm registered under the Companies Act, 1956/2013 or an Academic Institution accredited/affiliated to or recognized as a University or Deemed University by UGC Act. In case, the Applicant Agency is an NGO, then the Applicant Agency shall be registered on the DARPAN Platform- NITI Aayog and shall provide a Unique ID while submitting the proposal. The Applicant Agency shall comply with the following conditions:
   1. In case the Applicant Agency is NGO/Voluntary organization, the Applicant Agency shall provide documentary evidence (such as a Work Order/Letter of Award/Contract) of undertaking a road safety programme or any other similar activity of an advocacy nature (for grants-in-aid for programme).
   1. The Applicant Agency shall undertake assignment individually or associate with another Applicant Agency to form a JV (Joint Venture), the maximum number of members in the JV shall not exceed two (2). In the case of JV, the members shall appoint a Lead Member and the members agree to the terms and conditions jointly and severally.
   1. Only projects involving road safety activities or involving advocacy/ awareness on any social cause will be considered for arriving at the eligible maximum financial assistance.
   1. The Applicant Agency should have experience in completing at least one (1) road safety or advocacy/awareness-related program in the last three (3) years as of the date of submission of the proposal.
   1. The Applicant Agency should not have been blacklisted or debarred by any State/ Central Government Entities from receiving any funds.

scheme_name: Scheme For Grant Of Rewards To The Children Of Salt Labourers
scheme_name_original: Scheme For Grant Of Rewards To The Children Of Salt Labourers
description:
The scheme “Scheme for Grant of Rewards to the Children of Salt Labourers” was launched by Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT), Ministry of Commerce and Industry in the year 1985. Initially, the scheme known as “Scheme for grant of rewards to the children of labourers working in Salt Industry (CRS)” was initiated for granting 20 rewards to the children of the salt workers to enable them to meet the initial expenses either partly or wholly for purchase of books, stationeries, etc., on admission to recognized institutes for higher studies.
         Since 2011-12 the numbers of rewards are 3500 with a financial implication of ₹45.00 Lakh. Under the scheme, the financial assistance will be given as ₹1000/- for the students of classes VI to VIII, ₹1500/- for classes IX to X, and ₹2000/- for classes XI to XII with the proviso that awards for girl child be reserved to a minimum of 50% allocation per state. In the absence of female students in a particular Salt Factory/State, the reward could be given to the available eligible male students in each category of other Salt Factory/State.
benefits:
The rewards shall be granted once in each academic year to the meritorious children of salt workers to enable the students to meet the initial expenses either partly or wholly for the purchase of books, stationery, etc. on admission to a recognized Institute, recognized by the State/Central Government.
The rewards shall be granted to the students of the salt workers in cash, to be paid in one lump sum at the commencement of the academic year at the rates given below:

Student/Classes
Rewards in an academic year
Students of classes VI to VIII
₹1000/-
Students of classes IX to X
₹1500/-
Students of classes XI to XII 
₹2000/-
eligibility_summary:
1. The children of only those salt workers who have put in a minimum of one year of continuous service in any of the salt works &amp; passing from a recognized Government School are eligible to apply under the scheme.
   1. A child of a salt worker should be studying in Class VI to XII.
   1. A child of a salt worker to be eligible for a reward should have passed the examination in the first attempt.

**Note 01:** Preference will be given, other things being equal to the SC/ST/BC/Backward area applicants if applicants are both from either of these categories and the general category.
**Note 02:** The awards for girl children be reserved to a minimum of 50% allocation per state. In the absence of female students in a particular Salt Factory/State, the reward could be given to the available eligible male students in each category of other Salt Factory/State.

A certificate that the child has passed the Primary/Middle/Secondary/Higher Secondary School Certificate examination in the first attempt.
Certified copy of the mark sheet showing the marks obtained by the child of the salt worker at the said examination duly issued by the concerned Board.
Birth certificate of the applicant
Caste certificate
Bank account details/ Bank Pass Book
Certificate of the employer of the parents of the applicant
Residence proof, if any
application_process:
Application Process:
Step 01:
 A child of a salt worker, who desires to avail himself/herself of a reward, shall apply in the prescribed application form. The application form is available with 
Scheme Guideline (https://dpiit.gov.in/programmes-and-schemes/others/scheme-grant-rewards-children-salt-labourers)
 (Annexure) and can be downloaded from the 
Official website (https://dpiit.gov.in/)
.
Step 02:
 The completely filled application form along with all the supporting documents shall be sent to the Salt Commissioner, Jaipur through his/her employer, latest by the 31st day of July of the academic year in which the child has passed the Primary/Middle/Secondary/Higher Secondary School Certificate examination.
Note 01:
 Such applications shall be accompanied by a certificate from the employer of the salt worker specifying the date from which the salt worker has been in continuous service in the salt work.
Note 02:
 Such Applications shall also be accompanied by a certificate that the child has passed the Primary/Middle/ Secondary/Higher Secondary School Certificate examination in the first attempt and a certified copy of the mark sheet showing the marks obtained by the child of the salt worker at the said examination duly issued by the concerned Board. 
Scrutiny of Application:
Step 01:
 All applications received by the Regional Officer shall be properly scrutinized by him and the Regional Officer shall submit them to the Salt Commissioner with suitable recommendations for grant of rewards.
Step 02:
 The Regional officer shall process all such applications and submit them to the Salt Commissioner, Jaipur with his recommendations, latest by the 20th August, of the academic year.
Note:
 For such scrutiny and recommendation, the Regional Officer shall be guided strictly by merit as indicated by the percentage of marks obtained by the applicant in the Primary/Middle/Higher Secondary/School Certificate examination in that academic year.
Selection Process:
On receipt of an application, with recommendations of the Regional Officer, the Salt Commissioner shall scrutinize all the applications and decide the case in which rewards shall be granted.
Note 01:
 The Salt Commissioner will be guided by the merit of applications and the recommendations of the Regional Officer in each case.
Note 02:
 The Salt Commissioner’s decision in the matter of grant of rewards shall be final and no correspondence or appeal shall lie against his decision to give reward.

Accelerated new planting/replanting would be achieved by giving proper technical guidance and financial assistance to growers.

eligibility_summary:
> **Traditional** 1. The growers owning rubber areas not exceeding 2.00 ha shall be eligible for assistance under Rule VI of the scheme. 1. The planting grant payable will be limited to an area of 1.00 ha. 1. The growers who undertake new planting/replanting rubber in a minimum area of 0.10 ha will be eligible for assistance. 1. The applicant should have absolute possession over the land in respect of which assistance is sought. 1. Areas notified/certified in the documents as paddy fields are not eligible for any kind of assistance under this scheme.
> **Non-Traditional and North Eastern Region** 1. The growers owning rubber areas not exceeding 5.00 ha shall be eligible for assistance under Rule VI of the scheme. 1. The planting grant payable will be limited to an area of 2.00 ha. 1. The growers who undertake new planting/replanting rubber in a minimum area of 0.10 ha will be eligible for assistance. 1. The applicant should have absolute possession over the land in respect of which assistance is sought. 1. Areas notified/certified in the documents as paddy fields are not eligible for any kind of assistance under this scheme.
> **Other Terms & Conditions** 1. The prescribed minimum stand of rubber plants (@450/ha) should be maintained and growth should be satisfactory as assessed by the inspecting officer. 1. The number of non-rubber trees, that already exist in the plantation can be retained in a proportion of 20 trees or 40 coconut palms or 80 Arecanut palms per ha, in a well-distributed manner. 1. Sloppy lands should be protected from soil erosion by contour terracing or construction of contour bunds or digging silt trenches or silt pits and also by planting of cover crops. 1. Boundary protection measures should be adopted. 1. The absolute right to refuse assistance without assigning any reason is vested with the Executive Director of the Rubber Board.

scheme_name_original: Scheme for Promotion of Culture of Science: Digital Planetarium/Space And Astronomy Education Centre (Category 1, Category 2 And Category 3)
description: The component "Digital Planetarium/Space and Astronomy Education Centre" under the Scheme for Promotion of Culture of Science by the Ministry of Culture, Government of India aims to create awareness about the sky, space and celestial phenomena, to integrate astronomy education with physical, mathematical and weather science, and to help eradicate superstitions associated with celestial bodies and phenomena. Through this component, financial assistance towards capital cost and corpus fund is provided under three categories to State Governments, Union Territories, and the Societies or Authorities promoted by the State or Union Territory Governments. The Digital Planetarium or Space and Astronomy Education Centre is being added as a new component in the scheme to enhance the Science Centre experience for students and the general public, and it may be co-located in the existing science centres or could be set up in any institution of non-formal learning engaged in science communication activities. The principal objective is twofold, namely to provide a fundamental concept about the celestial bodies, cosmic events and space science, and to alleviate superstitions and misconceptions about planets, stars, eclipses and so forth. The component is implemented by the National Council of Science Museums. > **Objectives:** - To introduce the sky to the students and the general public, with its innumerable celestial objects and their movement, and thus to create an awareness about astronomy. - To develop an understanding about the sky and the space and about the celestial phenomena. - To integrate the astronomical knowledge with that of physics, mathematics, weather science, artificial satellites and so forth. - To nurture scientific temper by eradicating superstitions related to astronomical objects and events like planets, sun, moon and eclipses. - To correlate our heritage and culture with science.

Conditions Associated with the Benefits:

Under Type B funding, the capital cost for Digital Planetarium/Space and Astronomy Education Centre Category 1, Category 2 and Category 3 is shared 50:50 for all locations other than North East including Sikkim, and 90:10 for the North Eastern Region including Sikkim. The corpus fund is shared 20:80.
The Digital Planetarium could be operated and managed under Type A, Type B and Type C, as detailed for science centres.
Under Type C, the State Governments and Union Territories shall fully fund the project and set it up with technical support from the National Council of Science Museums against payment of consultancy charges.
The corpus fund shared by the Government of India shall in no case exceed 20 per cent of the total Corpus Fund; the principal shall in no case be utilized for any activity; not more than 85 per cent of the interest can be utilised to meet the operational deficit after inauguration, and a minimum of 15 per cent is to be added back to compensate the inflation on a year to year basis.
The share of corpus fund of the Government of India and the State Government or Union Territory is to be released upfront after approval of the project and prior to commencement of the works.
The recurring expenditure will be completely borne by the State Government. Every year, provision for the annual recurring expenditure for maintenance of the equipment and organizing new planetarium shows shall be made by the State Government.
For Hilly Region, Island Territory and North Eastern Region, 20 per cent extra on the entire Capital Cost has been considered.
The building construction cost is considered based on normal foundation. If any special foundation is required to be done based on the Soil Test Report, the additional cost will have to be borne by the State Government.
Escalation of project cost shall be governed by successive cost index over DPAR-2019 as published by the Central Public Works Department at the time of the project work; the extra project cost on this account is to be borne by the State Government or Local Authority.
Content and Facilities Provided:

Category 1:
 Main Opto-mechanical Star field Projector capable of projecting 8,500 stars down to 6.5 magnitude on a tilted or horizontal Projection Dome; the Projector will have Space or Earth mode system, or a Full dome digital planetarium projector system, or both, depending upon available fund. Dome Size 12 metre diameter; Seating Capacity 120 to 125 unidirectional. The capital cost includes Civil and allied works ₹4.02 crore; Chairs ₹0.15 crore; Air Conditioning of Planetarium theatre and exhibition areas only ₹0.50 crore; Carpet in planetarium theatre ₹0.06 crore; Firefighting System ₹0.25 crore; Pure Digital Full-dome solution with High Contrast Light Emitting Diode or Solid State light source projection system with effective resolution of 4.5K after blending, including cost of 12.0 Metre Diameter inner Aluminium Dome ₹10.00 crore; Uninterruptible Power Supply ₹0.15 crore; Telescope and accessories for sky observations ₹1.00 crore; Office furniture, furnishing and tools ₹0.25 crore; Exhibits on Astronomy within the circular passage around the planetarium theatre with exhibition space of 350 Square Metres approximately ₹1.00 crore; Transportation, Installation and Commissioning of Exhibits at site ₹0.20 crore; Travelling Allowance or Daily Allowance, Training and Miscellaneous Expenditure ₹0.20 crore; and Architects Fee ₹0.22 crore.
Category 2

Category 3:
 Mini Digital Projection System. Dome Size 8 metre diameter; Seating Capacity 50 unidirectional. Special Effect Projectors and Attachments; Complete sound system for the Planetarium Theatre; Projection dome; and Cove lights.
Additional Facilities for Category 1 and Category 2:
 Interactive exhibition on astronomy and space science; Activity area for students on astronomy; Sky observation through a Global Positioning System-enabled telescope; Lecture hall for astronomy lectures by specialists; and Office, maintenance workshop, and show development room.
Additional Facilities for Category 3: 
Activity area for students on astronomy; Sky observation through a Global Positioning System-enabled telescope; Lecture hall for astronomy lectures by specialists; and Office, maintenance workshop and show development room.
Mode of Disbursement:

Normally, the digital planetarium will be set up by the National Council of Science Museums on a turn-key basis, including construction and commissioning of the equipment, and handed over after completion to the State Government or Union Territory. The construction work shall start only after the share or funding is received from the State or Union Territory Government. Recurring Expenditure and Projected Revenue:

Category 1: Recurring expenditure of ₹50,00,000 per annum, comprising ₹30,00,000 salary, ₹15,00,000 maintenance and ₹5,00,000 activities and spares approximately, for operating the planetarium, shall be borne by the agency or society running the Planetarium or by the State Government. Considering 60 per cent occupancy, that is 60 per cent public and 40 per cent students, and 5 shows a day, revenue from tickets would be ₹19.44 lakh per year from the public (60 per cent of 360 persons a day at ₹30 per person for 300 days in a year) and ₹8.64 lakh per year from students (40 per cent of 360 students a day at ₹20 per student for 300 days in a year), totalling ₹28.08 lakh per year.

eligibility_summary: 1. The applicant should be a State Government, a Union Territory, or a Society or Authority promoted by the State or Union Territory Government. 1. The applicant proposing a Category 1 Digital Planetarium should propose a location fulfilling the criteria for Science Centre – Category 1, that is, a city or town with a population of 15,00,000 or more, and the planetarium shall have a 12 metre dome. 1. The applicant proposing a Category 2 Digital Planetarium should propose a location fulfilling the criteria for Science Centre – Category 2, that is, a city or town with a population between 5,00,000 and 15,00,000, and the planetarium shall have a 10 metre dome. 1. The applicant proposing a Category 3 Digital Planetarium should propose a location fulfilling the criteria for Science Centre – Category 3, that is, a city, town or location with a population of less than 5,00,000, and the planetarium shall have an 8 metre dome. 1. The applicant proposing a Category 1 Digital Planetarium should provide a minimum of 2.0 acres of land, or 1.0 acre if the Planetarium is located inside the Science Centre Campus. 1. The applicant proposing a Category 2 Digital Planetarium should provide a minimum of 2.0 acres of land, or 1.0 acre if the Planetarium is located inside the Science Centre Campus. 1. The applicant proposing a Category 3 Digital Planetarium should provide a minimum of 1.0 acre of land. 1. The applicant may either collocate the Centre with an existing Science Centre, or attach it to one, or set it up independently in another non-formal educational institution which is engaged in science popularization activities. 1. The applicant State Government or Union Territory should give a commitment to provide free land and funds as per norms. 1. The applicant should employ adequate professional staff for the operation and management of the Digital Planetarium. 1. The applicant should ensure that all buildings constructed under the scheme are designed keeping applicable fire safety norms of the location and the National Building Code. 1. The applicant should form a Registered Society immediately after the release of the fund by the State Governments or Union Territories towards their share of the capital cost of the project. 1. The applicant should sign a Memorandum of Understanding with the National Council of Science Museums for implementation of the project, if undertaken and implemented by the National Council of Science Museums. > **Preference, Priority and Relaxation:** - The land requirement is relaxed to 1.0 acre for Category 1 and Category 2 if the Planetarium is located inside the Science Centre Campus. - The Digital Planetarium is to be preferably co-located in the existing Science Centres, science museums or non-formal education institutions that promote science communication, especially astronomy education. - Preferably, the State Government, Union Territory, or agency shall undertake the construction of the building within the allocated budget, with inputs and supervision from the National Council of Science Museums. - The eligibility criteria of population, land, funding pattern, and feasibility and financial viability of the project considering the intangible outcome of the facility in terms of knowledge gain may be relaxed and/or modified in special cases or circumstances by the Honourable Chief Minister, Government of India, as stated in the document. - In the construction of the building, priority or preference may be given to local material, labour and expertise; wherever possible, community participation may be encouraged; use of renewable energy and energy-saving devices may be given top preference.

description: The component "Innovation Hubs" under the Scheme for Promotion of Culture of Science by the Ministry of Culture, Government of India aims to redefine the usage and role of existing science facilities in fostering problem-solving and project-based learning, and to provide hands-on and practical learning and engagement in the process of science, technology and innovation. Through this component, financial assistance towards capital cost and recurring cost for the first three years is provided to State Governments, Union Territories, Societies and institutions, on a 50:50 sharing basis. Innovation Hubs would be co-located in existing Science Cities/Science Centres, science museums and non-formal educational institutions that promote creativity and inspire innovations; this co-location would promote more effective utilisation of these centres. The hubs would serve as springboards for new ideas and innovation, thus helping society and the economy to face future challenges and meet rising aspirations of the growing population. The component is implemented by the National Council of Science Museums. > **Objectives:** - To equip and strengthen activities of the existing Science Cities/Science Centres/institutions to inspire innovations by young children. - To catalyse creation of more innovation hubs in different parts of the country, especially in rural areas. - To provide an appropriate environment to nurture creative and innovative ideas of young children.

Conditions Attached to the Benefit:

The total project cost is to be shared in the ratio 50:50 between the State/Union Territory Government and the Ministry of Culture, Government of India, and this includes the recurring cost of Innovation Hubs.
The capital cost for setting up a new Innovation Hub shall be ₹2.60 crore under Category 1; in case built-up space of approximately 300 square metres is available under Category 2, the capital cost would be ₹1.50 crore.
There is no Corpus Fund for Innovation Hubs, but a recurring grant is given for the initial three years.
The recurring cost for the first three years is at ₹10,00,000/- per year per hub as the 50 per cent share of the Ministry of Culture, Government of India, after opening of the Innovation Hub; the balance 50 per cent is to be borne by the State Governments/Union Territories/Society.
The expected expenditure after inauguration of the Innovation Hub is ₹20,00,000/- per year. The share of recurring cost of the Government of India shall be available for the initial three years of operation as an incentive under the Scheme. After the initial three years of operation, the State Government/Union Territories/institutions will undertake to continue the activities.
The State Governments/Union Territories/Society/institutions have to bear the gap funding and the recurring cost thereafter.
The recurring expenditure, including the salary component, will be completely borne by the respective organisations. NCSM shall train the staff members on operation and maintenance of the Innovation Hubs.
Facilities Created Under the Component:
Approximately 300 square metres built-up area would be required for setting up the following facilities:

Innovation Hubs Facilities
Space Requirement (Approx.)
Objective/Contents/Activities
Discovery Hall
100 M²
This area will have 10 to 15 interactive science exhibits/experiments to create excitement about science through exploration and discovery of underlying principles. This will help promote logical thinking. 
Innovation Resource Centre and Hall of Fame - 
Celebrating Inventions & Innovation
50 M²
This space will be used to showcase innovative ideas/products/implements that have transformed our world or have made a significant impact on the way we conduct our lives, along with respective inventors & innovators. Stories or inspirations behind such innovations/inventions will also be mentioned through appropriate modes. Besides these, implements/ samples of appropriate technology and traditional knowledge systems, art and craft, and other areas of importance in public life in the respective regions shall be exhibited.
Idea Lab (Innovation Laboratory) with the following components:          - ThodPhod Jod (Break & Remake) Corner                     - Kabbad Se Jugad (Build from scraps)                           - Idea Box
100 M²
This lab will have the necessary basic facilities to pursue creative and innovative hobbies/activities that involve model making, basic science experimentation, design & fabrication of useful gadgets for practical use, teaching/learning kits or aids for better classroom transactions, and testing of samples like soil, water, food items, etc.                       Students learn to do things with their own hands, dismantle, reassemble and remake devices/gadgets. Students learn more by doing things practically using day-to-day scrap. Students generate their own innovative ideas and create an idea bank. The best ideas are chosen for experimentation/model making/project work.
Design Studio
50 M²
Mentors/Guides
At least one dedicated mentor on a contract basis. Additional mentoring support may be provided by NCSM centres.
As far as possible, each institution shall try to provide mentoring and guidance support for innovation activities in its own centres. But that may not always be possible, and hence external experts in different fields will also be engaged on an honorarium basis. It would, however, be appropriate to engage on a contract basis at least one core mentor, who shall be primarily responsible for coordinating and conducting the innovation centre activities.
Mode of Disbursement:

The State Governments/Union Territories/Institutions shall do the construction of the building/space for the Innovation Hub as per inputs from NCSM. NCSM shall provide technical and professional support at cost and consultancy charges to the State/Union Territory Government for the project.
Expected Time of Completion:

Completion time from the date of issue of Letter of Intent for the construction work – 24 months.
The time required for implementation of the Innovation Hub project will be 24 months from the start of the construction work where space is to be created, and 18 months where no space is required to be created.

Validity/Post-Sanction Obligations: 
After opening, the Innovation Hub should strive to enrol at least 300 active innovation members annually; increase the number of exposure visits to innovation hubs by school and college students and teachers to approximately 10,000 annually; file patents/copyrights on successful innovative prototypes; and set up at least 10 Innovation Clubs in nearby schools.

In addition, the Innovation Hubs should also strive to organize activities such as idea contests and innovation festivals including contests on design and idea challenges on local problems periodically; develop strong linkages with Indian Institutes of Technology, National Institutes of Technology, Universities, Research Institutions and Industry; and develop synergy with Atal Tinkering Labs by collaborating with such labs in schools and institutions across the country by way of exposure visits of student participants to the innovation hub facilities, sharing of success stories and training of mentors.

scheme_name_original: Scheme for Promotion of Culture of Science: Modernization/Up-gradation Of Existing Science Cities, Science Centres And Innovation Hubs
description: The component "Modernization/Up-gradation of Existing Science Cities, Science Centres and Innovation Hubs" under the Scheme for Promotion of Culture of Science by the Ministry of Culture, Government of India aims to provide grants and funds to modernise and upgrade, and to create a congenial spatial setting for diverse exhibitions, galleries and visitor amenities in the existing science cities, science centres and innovation hubs. Through this component, financial assistance up to a specified maximum ceiling is provided to those existing Science Cities, Science Centres and Innovation Hubs which were developed with funding from the Ministry of Culture, Government of India, or developed by the State Governments and Union Territories with full funding. India has over 50 to 60 Science Museums, Centres and Cities functioning in different States and Union Territories, of which 49 have been developed by the National Council of Science Museums since 1959; 25 centres are managed by the National Council of Science Museums and the remaining 24 have been handed over to the respective States, Union Territories and Societies for operation and management. The existing science museums and centres developed in the past have varying architecture, facilities, content and infrastructure, some of which do not conform to the prevailing trends in the world; with rapid development in science and technology, communication techniques and digital technologies, the Science Centres and Cities require modernization and up-gradation commensurate with the modern trends and requirements. The Modernization or Up-gradation plan may also include addition of a Mobile Science Exhibition unit to an existing Science City or Science Centre. The component is implemented by the National Council of Science Museums.

Facilities That May Be Added Under Modernization/Up-gradation:

The existing science cities and science centres may be modernised or upgraded with the following facilities, subject to availability of space and spare land, within the funds sanctioned under the scheme:

Modernization of Galleries, Exhibitions, Halls, Science Parks and visitors' amenities.
Addition of galleries on frontier areas of Science and Technology and topics related to current issues in Science.
Digital panoramic thematic presentations based on important scientific topics as well as on science and culture inter-relationship.
Addition of open labs on Frontier Areas of Science and Technology to provide real scientific exploration by the public.
Presentations on social issues with scientific solutions after proper contextualization.
Addition of virtual and immersive experiences.
Creation of new facilities such as Tropical Forests, Outdoor Amphi-Theatre, Solar powered park, Holography theatre, Hall of Fame to celebrate inventions and inventors, Digitally recreated archaeological sites, Spark Theatre, Dark Rides, Simulators, Robotics corner, 3D facility and Interpretation centres.
Addition of a mobile science exhibition van or bus on a suitable theme for travelling in rural and nearby region of the location.
Conditions Associated with the Benefit:

The actual budget will depend upon the facilities identified for up-gradation and modernization.
In no case shall the funds provided under the Modernization or Up-gradation scheme be utilized for acquiring land or an office vehicle for the Science Centre or City.
The Modernization or Up-gradation plan may also include addition of a Mobile Science Exhibition unit to an existing Science City or Science Centre.
The National Council of Science Museums shall be paid normal consultancy fees for execution of the project, or for the purpose where the project is implemented by the concerned Societies.
All buildings constructed under the scheme should be designed keeping applicable fire safety norms of the location and the National Building Code.
Mode of Disbursement:

The project shall normally be undertaken by the National Council of Science Museums on a turn-key basis. The funds for the project will be received by the National Council of Science Museums, both from the Central Government and the State Governments, Union Territories and Societies. The National Council of Science Museums shall take up the modernization or up-gradation of the Science Cities, Centres and Innovation Hubs on its own, or through Creative Museum Designers, a wholly owned Section 25 company of the National Council of Science Museums.
In case of a State or Union Territory Government, or the Societies formed by the State or Union Territory Governments, seeking financial support from the Government of India for a modernization or up-gradation project to be implemented by the concerned Societies, the project will be vetted and processed by the National Council of Science Museums for approval of the competent authority in the Ministry of Culture, Government of India.
Frequency of Disbursement:

In such a case, funds will be released by the Ministry of Culture, Government of India, to the State Government or Union Territory, or to the Societies, in a phased manner, subject to sanction and release of the State or Union Territory's share of funds from the respective State or Union Territory Governments and Societies, and submission of the utilization certificate by the State or Union Territory Government and Societies for the funds released from the Government of India and the State Governments, Union Territories and Societies.
Expected Time of Completion:

The maximum project or scheme completion time is 36 months for a Science City, 24 months for Science Centres Category 1 and Category 2, 18 months for Science Centres Category 3, and 12 months for Innovation Hubs.

application_process:
Step 1:
 The existing Science City, Science Centre, or Innovation Hub should have completed at least 5 years of operation and have satisfactory performance.
Step 2: 
Identify the facilities proposed for modernization or up-gradation from the list at 
Annexure G (https://culture.gov.in/files/inline-documents/Revised_Guidelines_of_SPoCS_08_11_2021.pdf)
.
Step 3: 
Obtain the Application Form for Grants-in-aid for Modernization of existing Science City, Science Centres or Innovation Hubs and the Detailed Project Report format, both enclosed at 
Annexure H (https://culture.gov.in/files/inline-documents/Revised_Guidelines_of_SPoCS_08_11_2021.pdf)
.
Step 4: 
Fill the application form with the name and complete address of the organization, availability of built up space, category applied for, organization's profile, details of income from other sources including foreign sources during the last three financial years, estimated cost of the facility, details of own resources, amount of grant-in-aid sought, details of grants-in-aid sought or received from other bodies, location of site, past experience in related activities, details of projects taken up in the last 10 years, and organization and management of work.
Step 5: 
Prepare the Detailed Project Report as per 
Annexure H (https://culture.gov.in/files/inline-documents/Revised_Guidelines_of_SPoCS_08_11_2021.pdf)
, preferably as a hard bound volume in A4 size in portrait alignment, with drawings in A3 size integrated as a foldout within the volume. Drawings, details, views, sketches and supporting photographs may also be submitted in addition on a Compact Disc, Digital Versatile Disc or Pen Drive. An incomplete Detailed Project Report will render the application liable for rejection.
Step 6:
 Attach the mandatory documents as listed above.
Step 7: 
Certify that the information given is correct, and sign the form as applicant or Head of Organization with name in block letters, designation and office stamp.
Step 8:
 Submit the proposal with the Detailed Project Report to:
Joint Secretary (Museums)
Ministry of Culture, Government of India,
Shastri Bhawan, New Delhi-110001
Step 9: 
The Detailed Project Report shall be evaluated and vetted by the National Council of Science Museums, or by a committee constituted by the Ministry of Culture with representation from the National Council of Science Museums. Where the project is to be implemented by the concerned Societies, the project will be vetted and processed by the National Council of Science Museums for approval of the competent authority in the Ministry of Culture, Government of India.
Step 10: 
Obtain approval from the Government of India for modernization of the existing science city, centre or innovation hub under the scheme.
Step 11: 
Sign the Memorandum of Understanding between the National Council of Science Museums and the State Government, Union Territory or Society for implementation of the Project.
Step 12:
 Where the project is implemented by the National Council of Science Museums, funds are received by it from both the Central Government and the State Governments, Union Territories and Societies. Where implemented by the Societies, funds are released by the Ministry of Culture, Government of India, to the State Government, Union Territory or Societies in a phased manner, subject to sanction and release of the State or Union Territory's share and submission of the utilization certificate.
Step 13:
 The National Council of Science Museums shall take up the modernization or up-gradation on its own, or through Creative Museum Designers, a wholly owned Section 25 company of the National Council of Science Museums, on a turnkey basis.
Step 14: 
Complete the project within the maximum completion time, that is, 36 months for a Science City, 24 months for Science Centres Category 1 and Category 2, 18 months for Science Centres Category 3, and 12 months for Innovation Hubs.
Jurisdiction: 
All disputes arising out of the scheme shall be subject to the jurisdiction of the Courts of Delhi and New Delhi only.

description: The component "Science Centres - Category-I, Category-II, Category-III" under the Scheme for Promotion of Culture of Science by the Ministry of Culture, Government of India aims to provide the scope of "doing science" by adopting a hands-on approach, offering the visitor a number of experimental options through which they can discover scientific concepts themselves. Through this component, financial assistance towards capital cost and corpus fund is provided to State Governments, Union Territories, and the Societies/Authorities promoted by them, under three categories based on the population of the city or town. This mode of education has so far proved to be very effective in supplementing formal science education in the country. The component is implemented by the National Council of Science Museums. > **Objectives:** - To portray the growth of science and technology and their application in industry and human welfare, with a view to developing a scientific attitude and temper. - To create awareness and enhance public understanding, appreciation and engagement of the public in the process of Science and Technology. - To popularise science and technology by organising exhibitions, seminars, popular lectures, science camps and various other programmes. - To supplement science education given in schools and colleges, and to organise out-of-school educational activities. - To design, develop and fabricate science museum exhibits, demonstration equipment and scientific teaching aids. - To organise training programmes for science teachers, students, young entrepreneurs, technicians, physically challenged persons, housewives and others.

Conditions Attached to the Benefit:

Under Type A funding, for Science Centres to be set up in locations/regions where Science Centre activities have not yet started, or in priority areas, the Ministry of Culture may consider providing full funding for such Centres through NCSM. In no case will more than one Science Centre be set up in any State/Union Territory in future under the scheme. In States/Union Territories where NCSM centres already exist, such provision shall not be applicable.
Under Type B funding, the capital cost for a Science Centre (Category 1, 2 and 3) is shared on a 50:50 basis, except for the North Eastern Region including Sikkim, where it is shared on a 90:10 basis. The corpus fund is shared 20:80.
Under Type C funding, the State Government/Union Territory fully funds the project and sets it up with technical support from NCSM against payment of consultancy charges.
The corpus fund meets the operational deficit funding. The principal shall in no case be utilised for any activity. Not more than 85 per cent of the interest can be utilised to meet the operational deficit after inauguration, and a minimum of 15 per cent is to be added back to the corpus fund.
Pile foundation, if required, will be considered after getting the Soil Test Report; the additional cost is entirely borne by the State Government.
Third-party quality assurance charges at 1 per cent of the estimated cost are entirely borne by the State Government.
Escalation of project cost is governed by the successive cost index over DPAR-2019 as published by the Central Public Works Department.
The Mobile Science Exhibition bus facility will be added to the Science Centre only on allotment of a separate budget by the State Government/Union Territory.
Indicative Break-up of the Capital Cost:

Category I:
 Expenditure on Building construction works – Grand Total ₹23.07 crore, for a Science Centre of 4,000 square metres minimum. Expenditure on Exhibits, Equipment and Stores – Grand Total ₹8.43 crore, which includes three thematic galleries of approximately 600 square metres with 50 exhibits each (₹3.75 crore), Science Park of approximately 4 acres with pathway and 50 required exhibits (₹1.00 crore), inflatable dome planetarium system called Taramandal (₹0.10 crore), fully functional exhibit development laboratory (₹0.25 crore), other facilities like Computer training area, Library, Conference Room, Stores and Office (₹0.80 crore), training of required staff members and other miscellaneous expenses (₹0.15 crore), 3D theatre facility with equipment and furniture (₹1.00 crore), miscellaneous building or auditorium furnishing, signage and murals (₹0.25 crore), and salary and Travelling Allowance/Daily Allowance of project staff (₹1.130 crore). Corpus Fund at 30 per cent of the project cost.
Category 2: 
Expenditure on Building construction works – Grand Total ₹12.60 crore, for a Science Centre of 2,000 square metres minimum. Expenditure on Exhibits, Equipment and Stores – Grand Total ₹4.50 crore, which includes two thematic galleries of approximately 250 square metres with 25 exhibits (₹2.00 crore), Science Park of approximately 3 acres with pathway and required exhibits (₹0.80 crore), inflatable dome planetarium system (₹0.10 crore), fully functional exhibit development laboratory (₹0.20 crore), other facilities like Computer training area, Library, Conference Room, Stores and Office (₹0.40 crore), and salary and Travelling Allowance/Daily Allowance of project staff (₹1.00 crore). Mode of Disbursement:

For a Science Centre set up under 
Type A
 and 
Type B
, NCSM will complete the Science Centre on a turn-key basis, including construction and commissioning, and hand over the project after completion to the State Government/Union Territory. NCSM shall start the construction work only after the share of funding is received from the State/Union Territory Government.
For a Science Centre set up under 
Type C
, the State Government/Union Territory shall do the construction of the building as per inputs from NCSM and develop the Science Park as per the advice of NCSM. NCSM shall provide technical and professional support at cost and consultancy charges to the State/Union Territory Government for the project.
Frequency of Disbursement — Year-wise Utilization of Capital Expenditure:
Category 1: 40 per cent in the first year, 40 per cent in the second year and 20 per cent in the third year:

All locations other than North East including Sikkim/hilly terrain and island territories: Government of India releases ₹6.30 crore, ₹6.30 crore and ₹3.15 crore, totalling ₹15.75 crore capital, plus a maximum corpus of ₹1.90 crore, making ₹17.65 crore. The State/Union Territory Government is to release ₹12.82 crore upfront, including the minimum share of corpus fund of ₹9.04 crore.
Hilly terrains and island territories other than the above: Government of India releases ₹7.56 crore, ₹7.56 crore and ₹3.78 crore, totalling ₹18.90 crore capital, plus a maximum corpus of ₹2.26 crore, making ₹21.16 crore. The State/Union Territory Government is to release ₹27.94 crore upfront, including the minimum share of corpus fund of ₹9.04 crore.

Category 2:
40 per cent in the first year, 40 per cent in the second year and 20 per cent in the third year:

All locations other than North East, including Sikkim: Government of India releases ₹3.42 crore, ₹3.42 crore and ₹1.71 crore, totalling ₹8.55 crore capital, plus a maximum corpus of ₹1.03 crore, making ₹9.58 crore. Hilly terrains and island territories other than the above: Government of India releases ₹4.10 crore, ₹4.10 crore and ₹2.05 crore, totalling ₹10.25 crore capital, plus a maximum corpus of ₹1.24 crore, making ₹11.49 crore. The State/Union Territory Government is to release ₹15.21 crore upfront, including the minimum share of corpus fund of ₹4.96 crore.

Category 3:
60 per cent in the first year and 40 per cent in the second year:

All locations other than North East, including Sikkim: Government of India releases ₹1.53 crore and ₹1.02 crore, totalling ₹2.55 crore capital, plus a maximum corpus of ₹0.31 crore, making ₹2.86 crore. The State/Union Territory Government is to release ₹3.79 crore upfront, including the minimum share of corpus fund of ₹1.24 crore.
North East regions including Sikkim: Government of India releases ₹3.30 crore and ₹2.19 crore, totalling ₹5.49 crore capital, plus a maximum corpus of ₹0.37 crore, making ₹5.86 crore. The State/Union Territory Government is to release ₹4.53 crore upfront, including the minimum share of corpus fund of ₹1.48 crore.
Expected Time of Completion:

Completion time from the date of issue of Letter of Intent for the construction work: Category 1 – 42 months; Category 2 – 36 months; Category 3 – 30 months.
Project timeline from the date of placing of order for construction of building:
Category 1: Construction of Building – 27 months; Development of Science Park – 12 months; Fabrication of exhibits – 30 months; Installation of exhibits – 9 months after completion of other facilities; Opening of the centre – 42 months approximately.
Category 2: Construction of Building – 21 months; Development of Science Park – 12 months; Fabrication of exhibits – 24 months; Installation of exhibits – 6 months after completion of other facilities; Opening of the centre – 36 months approximately.
Category 3: Construction of Building – 21 months; Fabrication of exhibits – 18 months; Installation of exhibits/Innovation and creative corner facility – 8 months after completion of other facilities; Opening of the centre – 30 months approximately.
Validity/Post-Sanction Obligations:

Over a period of 5 years from opening, the Science Centre should strive to generate at least 50 per cent of its operating cost, achieve an annual visitors footfall of around 2,50,000 for Category 1 (2,00,000 for the North East Region), around 1,50,000 for Category 2 (75,000 for the North East Region) and around 30,000 for Category 3, and organize a minimum of 25 science communication activities annually, in-house and outreach.
eligibility_summary: 1. The applicant should be a State Government, a Union Territory, or a Society/Authority promoted by the State/Union Territory Government. 1. The applicant proposing a Category 1 Science Centre should locate it in a city or town with a population of 15,00,000 or more. 1. The applicant proposing a Category 2 Science Centre should locate it in a city or town with a population between 5,00,000 and 15,00,000. 1. The applicant proposing a Category 3 Science Centre should locate it in a city, town or location with a population of less than 5,00,000. 1. The applicant proposing a Category 1 Science Centre should provide a minimum of 7.0 acres of land. 1. The applicant proposing a Category 2 Science Centre should provide a minimum of 5.0 acres of land. 1. The applicant proposing a Category 3 Science Centre should provide a minimum of 2.0 acres of land. 1. The applicant should ensure that the land is preferably centrally located, easily accessible, fully developed, without any low-lying area, of fairly regular shape, and secured with a boundary wall without any encumbrances. 1. The applicant State Government/Union Territory should give a commitment to provide free land and funds as per norms. 1. The applicant should employ adequate professional staff for operation and management. 1. The applicant should obtain all other statutory clearances and approvals required by the local authorities. 1. The applicant should choose the land in consultation with, and with the approval of, NCSM. 1. The applicant should ensure that the land is free from all encumbrances and encroachment. 1. The applicant should ensure that electricity, water, sewerage connection and telecommunication facility are available in the nearby vicinity. 1. The applicant should ensure that the land has good road connectivity for easy access and transport. 1. The applicant should not change the land once offered; if any such incident is noticed after release of grant, the released amount shall be recovered with the applicable rate of interest. 1. The applicant should provide provisions for the solar rooftop in the Detailed Project Report. 1. The applicant should ensure that buildings are designed keeping in view applicable fire safety norms of the location and the National Building Code. 1. The applicant should sign a Memorandum of Understanding with NCSM for implementation, if the project is undertaken and implemented by NCSM. > **Preference/Priority/Relaxation:** - For Category 2 Science Centres in the North East region, hilly terrains and island territories, 2.5 to 3.0 acres of land will be acceptable provided the land has good vicinity and accessibility. - In case the land is located in the heart of the city where land availability is scarce, the land requirement may be relaxed in the case of science centres. The building may be constructed in multiple stories utilising the available Floor Space Ratio of the location. However, the Science Park shall be an integral part of the science centre. - Under Type B operational mode, State Governments/Union Territory administrations desirous of having more than one science centre, or wanting accelerated development of Science Centres, shall be given priority, provided they agree to bear the entire operating cost of the centre after it is developed and handed over to the States/Union Territories. - Under Type C, State Governments agreeing to fully fund the science centre project, provide land and other required facilities, and operate and manage them shall be accorded priority. - Under Type A, priority areas and locations/regions where Science Centre activities have not yet started may be considered for full funding from the Ministry of Culture. - The eligibility criteria of population, land, funding pattern, and feasibility and financial viability may be relaxed and/or modified in special cases/circumstances by the Honourable Chief Minister, Government of India, as stated in the document. - In construction, priority/preference may be given to local material, labour and expertise; use of renewable energy and energy-saving devices may be given top preference.

description: The component "Science City" under the "Scheme for Promotion of Culture of Science" by the Ministry of Culture, Government of India aims to create a popular tourist attraction at the location that provides an experiment-based immersive learning ambience to inculcate a spirit of inquiry, foster creative talent and create scientific temper in the community as a whole. Through this component, financial assistance towards capital cost and corpus fund is provided to State Governments, Union Territories, and the Societies/Authorities promoted by them. A Science City is characterised by its two-pronged channel of communication, namely exhibits and activities; while the exhibits, both indoor and outdoor, are mostly interactive, the demonstrations and training programmes are fully participatory and help children and adults alike to learn the basics of science through fun and enjoyment. It will be large in dimension with a focus on frontier areas of Science and Technology and edutainment, and shall be financially self-sustainable. The component is implemented by the National Council of Science Museums. > **Objectives:** - To portray the growth of science and technology and their application in industry and human welfare, with a view to developing a scientific attitude and temper. - To create awareness and enhance public understanding, appreciation and engagement of the public in the process of Science and Technology. - To popularise science and technology by organising exhibitions, seminars, popular lectures, science camps and various other programmes. - To supplement science education given in schools and colleges, and to organise out-of-school educational activities. - To design, develop and fabricate science museum exhibits, demonstration equipment and scientific teaching aids. - To organise training programmes for science teachers, students, young entrepreneurs, technicians, physically challenged persons, housewives and others.

Escalation of project cost is governed by the successive cost index over DPAR-2019 as published by the Central Public Works Department; the extra cost is borne by the State Government/local authority.
Indicative Break-up of the Capital Cost:

Expenditure on Building construction works:
 Grand Total ₹110.81 crore, which includes Science Centre building of 14,000 square metres minimum with indoor exhibition halls, internal electrification, external Light Emitting Diode lighting, water supply and sanitary installation, firefighting, car and bus parking, underground reservoir of 2,50,000 litres, lifts, escalators, air-conditioning, Diesel Generator set, Closed Circuit Television surveillance, chairs and carpet, contingency at 3 per cent as per Central Public Works Department norms, and architect fee.
Expenditure on Exhibits, Equipment and Stores:
 Grand Total ₹68.00 crore, which includes large format film projection unit with laser projectors and accessories (₹25.00 crore), simulator and 3D film theatre (₹4.00 crore), thematic exhibits for Face to Face with Science and Technology (₹8.00 crore), interactive exhibits for experimentation and curriculum supplement (₹2.00 crore), projection equipment for auditorium (₹1.00 crore) and for digital panorama with laser projectors (₹22.00 crore), workshop tools and machineries (₹1.00 crore), development of Science park exhibits (₹1.50 crore), salary of project staff (₹2.50 crore), Travelling Allowance/Daily Allowance for project staff (₹0.40 crore), other administrative expenses (₹0.40 crore), and advertisement and publicity (₹0.20 crore).
Corpus Fund for Operational Deficit funding after inauguration:
 at 30 per cent of the project cost.
Mode of Disbursement:

The project shall normally be undertaken by NCSM on a turn-key basis. The funds are received by NCSM, both from the Central Government and the State Governments/Union Territories. NCSM sets up the Science City and hands it over to the State Government/Society for operation and management.
In case a State/Union Territory Government seeks financial support for a project to be implemented by themselves, a society should be formed by the respective State/Union Territory Government, and funds will be released by the Government of India to the society based on the recommendations of a Project Implementation Committee constituted by the Ministry of Culture with representatives of the Ministry of Culture, NCSM, experts in the field and the State Government.
Frequency of Disbursement — Year-wise Utilization of Capital Expenditure:

For all locations other than North East including Sikkim/hilly terrain and island territories:
 15 per cent in the first year, 25 per cent in the second year, 25 per cent in the third year, 25 per cent in the fourth year, and 10 per cent in the fifth year. The Government of India releases ₹16.11 crore, ₹26.85 crore, ₹26.85 crore, ₹26.85 crore and ₹10.74 crore respectively, totalling ₹107.40 crore capital, plus a maximum corpus of ₹10.74 crore, making ₹118.14 crore. The State/Union Territory Government is to release ₹114.56 crore upfront prior to starting of the project, including the minimum share of corpus fund of ₹42.96 crore.
For North Eastern Region including Sikkim: 
The Government of India releases ₹29.00 crore, ₹48.33 crore, ₹48.33 crore, ₹48.33 crore and ₹19.33 crore, totalling ₹193.32 crore capital, plus a maximum corpus of ₹12.90 crore, making ₹206.22 crore. The State/Union Territory Government is to release ₹73.08 crore upfront, including the minimum share of the corpus fund of ₹51.60 crore.
For hilly terrains and island territories other than the above:
 The Government of India releases ₹19.33 crore, ₹32.22 crore, ₹32.22 crore, ₹32.22 crore and ₹12.89 crore, totalling ₹128.88 crore capital, plus a maximum corpus of ₹12.90 crore, making ₹141.78 crore. The State/Union Territory Government is to release ₹137.52 crore upfront, including the minimum share of corpus fund of ₹51.60 crore. 
The share of the corpus fund of the Government of India and the State Government/Union Territory is to be released upfront after approval of the project and prior to commencement of the works.
Expected Time of Completion:

Completion time from the date of issue of Letter of Intent for the construction work 60 months.
Project timeline from the date of placing of order for construction of building: Construction of building including space theatre, science exploration hall, panorama and so forth 48 months; Development of Entrance Plaza 12 months; Development of Science Park 36 months; Fabrication of exhibits 30 months; Installation of exhibits 12 months after completion of other facilities; Opening of the centre 60 months approximately.
Validity/Post-Sanction Obligations:

Over a period of 5 years from opening, the Science City should strive to generate at least 50 per cent of its operating cost, achieve an annual visitors footfall of around 10,00,000 (5,00,000 for the North East Region), and organize a minimum of 25 science communication activities annually, in-house and outreach, including activities on climate change, biodiversity, nature conservation, topical issues and skill development.
eligibility_summary: 1. The applicant should be a State Government, a Union Territory, or a Society/Authority promoted by the State/Union Territory Government. 1. The applicant should propose a location, preferably where no major Science Centre exists. 1. The applicant may alternatively propose upgradation of an existing science centre to a Science City in locations where footfall to the science centre is substantial. 1. The applicant may alternatively propose a separate Science City in a State capital or the largest city of the State, provided that the Science City is viable and financially self-sustainable. 1. The applicant should provide at least 25.0 acres of land; however, 30.0 acres would be preferable to do justice to exhibits and facilities, especially those requiring open spaces and future expansion. 1. The applicant should ensure that the land is preferably centrally located, easily accessible, fully developed, without any low-lying area, of fairly regular shape, and secured with a boundary wall without any encumbrances. 1. The applicant State Government/Union Territory should give a commitment to provide free land and funds as per norms. 1. The applicant should employ adequate professional staff for operation and management. 1. The applicant should obtain all other statutory clearances and approvals required by the local authorities of the Central Government, State Government, Union Territory Government or other bodies. 1. The applicant should choose the land in consultation with, and with the approval of, NCSM. 1. The applicant should ensure that the land is free from all encumbrances and encroachment. 1. The applicant should ensure that electricity, water, sewerage connection and telecommunication facilities are available in the nearby vicinity. 1. The applicant should ensure that the land has good road connectivity for easy access and transport. 1. The applicant should not change the land once offered; if any such incident is noticed after release of grant, the released amount shall be recovered from the organisation with the applicable rate of interest. 1. The applicant should provide provisions for the solar rooftop in the Detailed Project Report, which is mandatory for the implementing agency. 1. The applicant should ensure that buildings are designed keeping in view applicable fire safety norms of the location and the National Building Code. 1. The applicant should sign a Memorandum of Understanding with NCSM for implementation, if the project is undertaken and implemented by NCSM. 1. The applicant should form the Society before the start of execution of the project so that it is able to receive monetary grants from both Central and State/Union Territory Governments, private/corporate/industry sources, as well as raise loans from financial institutions.

application_process:
Step 1: 
Check basic criteria. Confirm the location criteria (preferably where no major Science Centre exists, or a State capital/largest city of the State, provided the Science City is viable and financially self-sustainable) and the land criteria of at least 25.0 acres, preferably 30.0 acres.
Step 2:
 Decide the funding type. Only Type B (shared 60:40, or 90:10 for the North Eastern Region including Sikkim; corpus fund 20:80) or Type C (full State funding with technical support from the National Council of Science Museums against consultancy charges). A Science City is not to be set up under Type A.
Step 3:
 Select the land with approval of the National Council of Science Museums. The land shall be chosen in consultation with, and with the approval of, the National Council of Science Museums, and cannot be changed later; otherwise the released amount shall be recovered with applicable interest.
Step 4:
 Obtain the format. The Detailed Project Report format is enclosed with the guidelines at 
Annexure E (https://culture.gov.in/files/inline-documents/Revised_Guidelines_of_SPoCS_08_11_2021.pdf)
, with 
Annexure E-1 (https://culture.gov.in/files/inline-documents/Revised_Guidelines_of_SPoCS_08_11_2021.pdf)
 for the Physical Report on Site.
Step 5: 
Prepare the Detailed Project Report. It should include the feasibility report, demand survey, commitment of land free of cost and recurring cost, projected footfall, and expected revenue generation. It will preferably be a hard-bound volume in A4 size in portrait alignment, with A3 drawings as foldouts. An incomplete Detailed Project Report will render the application liable for rejection.
Step 6:
 Attach mandatory documents: Copy of Registration, Memorandum of Association or Trust Deed, Letter of Support from State Government, Letter of Recommendation from District Authority, Authorisation Certificate, Commitments for space and operation, and Audited Statement of Accounts for last three years, along with the filled 
Annexure E-1 (https://culture.gov.in/files/inline-documents/Revised_Guidelines_of_SPoCS_08_11_2021.pdf)
 with Site Map, Google Map and Non-Encumbrance Certificate.
Step 7:
 Submit the proposal to 
Joint Secretary (Museums), Ministry of Culture, Government of India, Shastri Bhawan, New Delhi-110001
Step 8: 
Challenge method consideration. The proposal shall be considered on the basis of challenge method guidelines, as and when issued by the Government of India.
Step 9:
 Appraisal by the Project Appraisal Committee, comprising the Joint Secretary (Museums), Ministry of Culture; Director/Deputy Secretary (Museums), Ministry of Culture; Representative from the Integrated Finance Division, Ministry of Culture; Director General, National Council of Science Museums; and Director, National Council of Science Museums dealing with SPoCS.
Step 10:
 Approval from the Government of India is required for setting up the Science City. Population, land, funding pattern, and feasibility and financial viability may be relaxed in special cases.
Step 11: 
Sign the Memorandum of Understanding between the National Council of Science Museums and the State/Union Territory Government, if implemented by the National Council of Science Museums.
Step 12: 
Form the Society before the start of execution of the project, by the State/Union Territory Government in consultation with the National Council of Science Museums, so that it can receive grants and raise loans.
Step 13: 
Release funds and begin construction. Funds are received by the National Council of Science Museums from both Central and State Governments, where it implements the project on a turn-key basis; where the State implements it, funds are released to the society on the recommendations of a Project Implementation Committee. The corpus fund share is released upfront after approval and prior to commencement of works. The State/Union Territory Government releases ₹114.56 crore, ₹73.08 crore or ₹137.52 crore upfront depending on location.
Step 14:
 Recruit staff: 22 posts within 6 months of release of funds and 22 posts within two years, totalling 44 posts.
Step 15: 
Execute as per the timeline 60 months from the date of issue of Letter of Intent for the construction work.
Step 16:
 Monitoring by an Executive Council set up by the State/Union Territory Government with representation from the Ministry of Culture, the National Council of Science Museums, the State Government, private or corporate partners, and at least five eminent personalities.
Step 17: 
Handover and outcome evaluation. The National Council of Science Museums hands over the Science City to the State Government/Society for operation and management. Over 5 years from opening, it should generate at least 50 per cent of operating cost, achieve an annual footfall of around 10,00,000 (5,00,000 for the North East Region), and organise a minimum of 25 science communication activities annually.
